newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Kabila troops take Congo protesters away in trucks.
newsitem.headline: Kabila troops take Congo protesters away in trucks.

text.p: Troops in Kinshasa packed about 50 student protesters into trucks and said they were taking them back to the campus after stopping their demonstration against self-proclaimed President Laurent Kabila, witnesses said.
"I am acting under orders," said the troop commander, who called himself John. He said former soldiers of ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko's army were among the protesters.
About 50 other marchers were made to sit by the roadside with their hands on their heads, under heavy guard by soldiers of Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL).

The march was called to protest against the exclusion of veteran opposition politician Etienne Tshisekedi from Kabila's new government and the presence of foreign African troops, including Rwandans, within the AFDL army.
